steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Data types: int, float, bool, char, string; type casting; constants vs variables

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Selection: if/elif/else, switch/case (match in Python 3.10+); nested conditions

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Iteration: for (definite), while (indefinite), do-while (at least once); break/continue

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Functions: definition, call, parameters (positional, keyword, default), return, recursion

steps.title: Worked example
steps.body: Q: Write a function that reads a file of integers and returns the median --- Solution: def median_from_file(filename): with open(filename) as f: nums = sorted(int(line.strip()) for line in f if line.strip()) n = len(nums) if n == 0: return None mid = n // 2 return nums[mid] if n % 2 else (nums[mid-1] + nums[mid]) / 2

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: Write a program that validates email format using regex | Implement a recursive factorial function | Create a menu-driven calculator with functions

steps.title: Lesson plan
steps.body: Starter (5 min): Recall prior knowledge of programming fundamentals with quick questions. Teaching (15 min): Work through each of the learning objectives, explaining principles step by step. Key points review (5 min): Revisit the key points together, confirming understanding. Worked example (10 min): Model the example question: Write a function that reads a file of integers and returns the median. Solution: def median_from_file(filename): with open(filename) as f: nums = sorted(int(line.strip()) for line in f if line.strip()) n = len(nums) if n == 0: return None mid = n // 2 return nums[mid] if n % 2 else (nums[mid-1] + nums[mid]) / 2 Practice (10 min): Students attempt the practice questions independently; circulate and support. Plenary (5 min): Review answers and address misconceptions.
